verification.summary: I did not implement the classifier. Investigation of the mock GitHub server and output/accs.bash showed the ACCS hits routes and env vars that don't exist anywhere in the app, so no implementation of pnpm classify could ever make it pass.

mustFix.problem: src/mock-github/server.ts only registers ISSUE_COMMENTS_PATH = /^\/issues\/(\d+)\/comments\/?$/ (the flat route). There is no /repos/:owner/:repo/issues/:id/comments route — I confirmed this both by reading server.ts and by live curl (repo-scoped path 404s, flat path 200s). marker_present_on_github can therefore never see a comment, so every phase-1 and phase-2 marker assertion fails no matter what the classifier posts.

src/mock-github/main.ts binds to MOCK_GITHUB_PORT (default 4123), and GITHUB_API_BASE_URL is defined nowhere in .env.example or the app. Unless a real .env happens to set it correctly, the health-check loop polls the wrong port for 60s and fails before any classify pass runs.

GITHUB_OWNER has no producer anywhere in the codebase (not in .env.example, not read by any src file). Worse, GH_REPO falls back to the pre-existing GITHUB_REPO var, which src/issue-tracker/config.ts and .env.example both document as a combined "owner/repo" string substituted as one path segment elsewhere. If a real .env sets GITHUB_REPO that way, accs.bash's separate $GH_OWNER/$GH_REPO concatenation injects an extra slash and breaks the URL regardless of the comments-route issue above.

application.blocked: output/accs.bash constructs requests against a repo-scoped comments endpoint and a default port/env-var set that don't exist anywhere in src/mock-github or the rest of the app, so the check fails independent of how faithfully pnpm classify implements the enriched-spec's contract.
